Northern District of California

                                                       Defendant.
                                  13
                                              Bayerische Motoren Werke AG and BMW of North America, LLC seek a thirty-
                                  14
                                       day extension of time to respond to Defendant’s counterclaims. Mot. (dkt. 79). Defendant
                                  15
                                       opposes, preferring a stay pending appeal. Opp’n (dkt. 81). The Court agrees with
                                  16
                                       Defendant.
                                  17
                                              “Courts have inherent power to manage their dockets and stay proceedings.” Jenam
                                  18
                                       Tech, LLC v. Google LLC, 630 F. Supp. 3d 1208, 1211 (N.D. Cal. 2022) (internal citation
                                  19
                                       omitted). Indeed, courts routinely stay cases pending appellate resolution of key issues.
                                  20
                                       See, e.g., Aleisa v. Square, Inc., 493 F. Supp. 3d 806, 817 (N.D. Cal. 2020) (granting stay
                                  21
                                       pending Supreme Court decision). The Court determines that “it is efficient for its own
                                  22
                                       docket and the fairest course for the parties to enter a stay of an action before it, pending
                                  23
                                       resolution of independent proceedings which bear upon the case.” See Leyva v. Certified
                                  24
                                       Grocers of California, Ltd., 593 F.2d 857, 863 (9th Cir. 1979). This case is in its early
                                  25
                                       stages, appellate disposition would simplify key issues, and the resources of the parties and
                                  26
                                       the Court would be conserved. See Landis v. N. Am. Co., 299 U.S. 248, 255 (1936)
                                  27
                                       (requiring courts to “weigh competing interests and maintain an even balance”).
                                  28
                                         Case 3:26-cv-05274-CRB        Document 83         Filed 07/20/26   Page 2 of 2




                                   1          Accordingly, the Court DENIES the motion and stays the case pending appeal.
                                   2   The parties may move to reopen the stay if there are any new issues related to the
                                   3   injunctive relief the Court has already granted.
                                   4          IT IS SO ORDERED.
                                   5          Dated: July 20, 2026
                                                                                          CHARLES R. BREYER

                                                       Defendant.
                                  13
                                              Defendant Zync Inc. asks this Court to stay its order granting a preliminary
                                  14
                                       injunction against its proceedings before the International Trade Commission pending its
                                  15
                                       current appeal. Mot. (dkt. 58). The Court GRANTS Zync’s motion. The Court’s order is
                                  16
                                       stayed for 14 days to permit the Ninth Circuit time to conclude whether a stay is
                                  17
                                       warranted. See Nomadix, Inc. v. Guest-Tek Interactive Entmt. Ltd., No.
                                  18
                                       219CV04980ABFFMX, 2020 WL 3023308, at *3 (C.D. Cal. Apr. 24, 2020) (staying
                                  19
                                       preliminary injunction to give the Ninth Circuit a chance to consider a stay).
                                  20
                                              IT IS SO ORDERED.
